item.title: Purdue basketball returns to cold shooting form in loss to DePaul
item.description: FORT MYERS, Florida − The 3-point shooting slump Purdue basketball seemingly shot its way out of during a four-game winning streak returned once the Boilermakers left the friendly rims of Mackey Arena. A disastrous shooting showcase highlighted DePaul's 65-56 victory over Purdue (4-3) at the Fort Myers Tip-Off Classic at Suncoast Credit Union Arena. During its four-game winning streak, Purdue shot 40.5% from 3-point range. As was the case in losses to Gonzaga and Valparaiso to open the season, the Boilermakers couldn't find a way to win when the shots weren't going in. Purdue made 4 of 28 3-pointers (14.3%) and closed the game missing 10 straight shots. The Blue Demons (6-0) capitalized on Purdue's inability to make shots in a game that became evident early would be defined by defense. Purdue basketball turning point vs. DePaul Purdue played right into DePaul's hands, enduring a back alley fight the Blue Demons force opponents into. Once the Boilermakers embraced the physicality, they went on a 15-2 run with a spark from the bench while Daniel Jacobsen watched the final 16:38 of the first half on the bench with two fouls. Getting to halftime with a 33-32 lead without Jacobsen while turning the ball over eight times and shooting 9.1% from 3-point range came on Purdue playing rugged and dominating the rebounding. Purdue scored 11 second chance points in the first half. A 3-pointer by Koree Cotton gave DePaul the lead to start the second half and Purdue's struggles helped the Blue Demons stay in front. Purdue did come back to tie the game at 54 with 5:30 to go, but Jack Benter missed the second of two free throw attempts with a chance to give Purdue the lead. The Boilermakers missed 10 straight shots after that and watched a close game become a gap too big to recover from. Game MVP Layden Blocker's ability to get by Purdue defenders and convert at the rim was problematic for the Boilermakers all night. Blocker scored 16 points to go with 3 steals and 2 assists. 3 Purdue basketball standouts vs. DePaul Luke Ertel: The freshman is built for big moments and fresh off a game where he made 8 3-pointers in a win over Oakland , Ertel was lifting the Boilermakers through adversity with another big night. Foul trouble derailed it. Ertel scored a team-high 12 points. Raleigh Burgess: Without Jacobsen, Burgess played stellar defense off the bench in the first half. He had 4 points, 3 rebounds and an assist in nine minutes, helping the Boilermakers survive without their 7-foot-4 center. Gicarri Harris: The junior guard does so many little things that don't show up on a stat sheet. On top of that, he's also filling the box score. Harris finished with 11 points, 6 rebounds and a steal. Sam King covers sports for the Journal & Courier. Email him at sking@jconline.com and follow him on X and Instagram @samueltking. item.title: Singleton scores 22 as Iowa State opens Players Era Tournament with W
item.description: Tre Singleton (0) of the Iowa State Cyclones looks on before a game against the San Diego State Aztecs during the Players Era 16 bracket of The 2026 Players Era Men's Championship at Michelob ULTRA Arena on Nov. 24, 2026 in Las Vegas. | Zach Del Bello/Players Era LAS VEGAS – Tre Singleton scored a game-high 22 points and Dom Pleta hauled in a game-high 10 rebounds as Iowa State powered past San Diego State 81-68 Tuesday night. San Diego State held an early 8-7 lead at the first media timeout. Iowa State responded as Prather knocked down a 3-pointer to put the Cyclones ahead 13-10, followed immediately by a Singleton layup. That sequence capped a 12-2 run over 3:36, pushing Iowa State’s lead to 17-10. The Aztecs answered after Singleton was assessed a flagrant-1 foul. Luka Skorić sank a pair of free throws and Isaiah Sy hit a 3-pointer to trim the deficit to 17-15. Buchanan halted the momentum with a dunk to push the cushion back to four. Moments later, Prather sank three consecutive free throws and Singleton drilled a 3-pointer to extend the lead to double digits at 25-15. Iowa State later reeled off a 7-0 run over 95 seconds, building a 37-25 advantage with 3:16 left in the first half behind 11 early points from Singleton. Sy added a late layup for San Diego State, and after Pleta’s half-court heave missed at the horn, Iowa State carried a 41-34 lead into halftime. Singleton led all scorers with 14 points at the break. San Diego State trimmed the margin to two points early in the second half. A Taj Manning layup restored a 50-44 cushion, though Manning soon picked up his fourth foul. The Aztecs failed to capitalize, going 0-for-2 at the foul line following a lane violation, keeping Iowa State ahead 56-50 with 11 minutes remaining. The Cyclones seized full control from there. A Prather 3-pointer and two free throws from Singleton stretched the lead back to 11. Iowa State then mounted its fourth 7-0-or-better run of the night, scoring seven points in just 64 seconds to build a 71-57 cushion at the 5:18 mark. San Diego State center Bear Cherry fouled out with the Cyclones leading by 15 with 85 seconds remaining. Prather finished with 16 points. With the win, Iowa State advances to take on No. 9 Tennessee on Thursday.

item.title: Curt Cignetti will have nobody to blame but himself if Indiana misses out on College Football Playoff
item.description: Since Curt Cignetti became Indiana’s head coach, the Hoosiers have won 36 out of 40 games, been to the College Football Playoff twice, won a Big Ten title and hung a national championship banner in Memorial Stadium. Even now, long past the point of Indiana football’s new reality becoming normal, it’s a staggering achievement with almost no comparison in the history of sports. But even the best of the best have a blind spot. With Cignetti, it’s the schedule. It’s always the schedule. The CFP committee ranked Indiana No. 14 on Tuesday, putting the Hoosiers in a perilous position heading into the final week of the regular season. Though key results around the country will still impact the rankings, and the committee has made some surprising moves at the last minute before, here’s the tough part for Indiana: The only way to significantly improve their résumé is by getting into the Big Ten championship game and winning it, which would get them in the field automatically. Anything short of that will leave Indiana vulnerable. And it’s (mostly) their own fault. Or, to be more specific, it’s Cignetti’s fault for refusing to acknowledge that non-conference games are important. With Cignetti, it’s not that Indiana has a tough time getting a high-profile opponent to play them. It’s not a financial calculation. It’s a sneering, unserious contempt for any suggestion that Indiana has a responsibility as a premier program to play non-conference games that are worth watching. And now it might really cost him. “We figured we would just adopt the SEC’s scheduling philosophy,” Cignetti said at Big Ten media day before the 2025 season. “Some people don't like it. I'm more focused in on those nine conference games.” But what if those nine conference games don’t give you enough opportunities for good wins? Indiana coach Curt Cignetti reacts during the Hoosiers' overtime loss to Washington on Saturday. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Steph Chambers via Getty Images Indiana has had, by all measures, another outstanding season at 9-2. The Hoosiers lost at home to Ohio State because receiver Nick Marsh was barely out of bounds when he caught the would-be winning touchdown and then again last weekend at Washington because it went 1-for-3 on field goals and lost by three points in overtime. By the same token, Indiana has lived on the margins all season long, winning four one-score games and pulling off a couple unlikely comebacks. They’re probably right about where they should be. It’s not Indiana’s fault the Big Ten has had a strange year, but the selection committee can only judge what they see on tape. Besides a pretty good win over No. 15 Southern Cal, Indiana has nothing else to put in front of the committee and argue that it’s done enough to be in the CFP. item.title: Kevin Vallejos denies cheating at UFC Qatar, slams Aljamain Sterling – ‘Doesn’t know how to lose’
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - DECEMBER 07: Aljamain Sterling enters the Octagon in a featherweight bout during the UFC 310 event at T-Mobile Arena on December 07, 2024 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Chris Unger/Zuffa LLC) Red-hot Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Featherweight prospect Kevin Vallejos believes Aljamain Sterling is having trouble accepting his UFC Qatar loss. Vallejos scored the biggest victory of his career this past weekend (Sat., Nov. 21, 2026), defeating the former Bantamweight champion via unanimous decision inside ABHA Arena in Doha, Qatar. Two judges awarded Vallejos all three rounds, while the third scored the Featherweight co-main event 29-28. The fight was much closer than those scorecards suggest, however. Sterling outlanded Vallejos by one significant strike in each of the first two rounds, but “El Chino” connected with the more damaging shots and completely shut down Sterling’s wrestling. The former champion completed just one of his 12 takedown attempts across 15 minutes. Sterling believes he did enough to win, while fellow Featherweight contender Lerone Murphy labeled the decision a “robbery.” Vallejos can understand Sterling thinking he won a close fight, but he remains confident the judges reached the correct decision. “That’s fine that he feels like that,” Vallejos told Yahoo Sports!. “I mean, I feel like I won, but it wasn’t something that was super obvious. It was a super strategic fight.” “How I saw it was I completely neutralized his best weapons, which was his grappling, and even in the striking — it was close, but I won that,” he continued. “I hurt him more than he hurt me. So, I felt like I won the fight.” Sterling’s criticism did not stop with the scorecards. While reviewing the fight, “Funk Master” questioned how Vallejos repeatedly escaped deep takedown attempts, claiming he had never experienced an opponent slipping out of his grasp so easily. Sterling stopped short of directly accusing Vallejos of greasing but certainly floated the possibility. Vallejos did not appreciate the insinuation. “At the end of the day, I have a lot of respect for Aljamain Sterling, and to be honest, I feel like he completely disrespected me and my performance by saying that,” Vallejos said. “At the end of the day, he can feel bad about it or not, but he’s 37 years old, and he clearly doesn’t know how to lose.” “I specifically trained really hard to neutralize his grappling, and I did that,” he continued. “If he wants to make that excuse, that is fine, but that’s not how it was.” Vallejos also responded on social media, inviting Sterling to train in Argentina so he could learn the secrets behind his takedown defense. “We don’t need greasing,” Vallejos wrote. “We simply just get up.” Grease or no grease, the official result is not changing. item.title: Providence's shooting woes prove costly in Maui loss to No. 8 Arizona
item.description: Caleb Holt scored 21 points and Motiejus Krivas added 20 as No. 8 Arizona cruised to an 84-66 victory over Providence in the Maui Invitational semifinals on Tuesday, Nov. 24, in Lahaina, Hawaii. The Wildcats (6-1) will face Ole Miss, a 73-63 winner over No. 19 BYU, in Wednesday's tournament final. Arizona has won three previous Maui Invitational titles, including in its last appearance in 2022. Holt had his second straight 20-point performance and fourth of the season, making 6 of 9 shots from the field and 3 of 4 from 3-point range. Krivas was 7 of 9 from the field to go with seven rebounds, four blocks and three assists. Arizona has had at least one player score 20 or more points in every game this season. Ivan Kharchenkov contributed 15 points, six rebounds and eight assists as Arizona shot 51.9% overall and 10 of 19 from 3-point range. Providence (5-2), which had defeated VCU, 72-66, on Monday, got 22 points on 8-of-13 shooting from Ryan Mela, but the rest of the team was 17 of 52. The Friars were 7 of 28 from 3-point range. Arizona led 48-26 at halftime but Providence scored the first eight points of the second half. The Wildcats didn't make a field goal for nearly five minutes but then made three in a row to get the lead to 57-38. The Friars were 1 of 11 from 3-point range in the first half but started the second half 4 of 6 from deep. They got as close as 57-44 on an Elijah Saunders 3-pointer, but Arizona made 9 of 13 to go up, 74-52, with 7:51 to go. Holt scored nine consecutive points for Arizona as the Wildcats pushed their lead to 21-10 with 11:23 remaining in the first half. A subsequent 11-0 run, including seven straight by Krivas, extended the margin to 34-13. The Friars, who won the inaugural Maui Invitational in 1984, were set to face BYU in the third-place game on Wednesday afternoon. item.title: College Football Playoff rankings show’s inability to start on time adds to ongoing frustrations
item.description: Credit: ESPN Many people will tell you that the weekly College Football Playoff ranking show on ESPN only exists to cause arguments and get people mad. And if so, they do an amazing job. Every week, the new rankings are announced; there are at least one or two inexplicable decisions followed by unsatisfactory explanations , and then everyone in the college football world spends the next two days complaining about them . If that were it, it would be one of the most agonizing viewing experiences of any college football fan’s week. But there’s an extra wrinkle added to the weekly appointment that turns the annoyance and frustration up to 11: The dang show never starts on time . Tuesday’s rankings reveal, the fourth of the 2026 season, was scheduled to start at 7:30 p.m. ET. That didn’t happen because the Creighton-Michigan game beforehand ran long, and ESPN wasn’t going to cut away, even though it was a Bluejay blowout of the Wolverines. The rankings reveal didn’t actually get underway until 8:15 p.m. ET, a whopping 45 minutes later. Adding even more frustration, they’ll have to hustle because ESPN is set to air No. 23 Louisville vs. No. 9 Texas Tech immediately afterward. That game tips off at 8:00 p.m. ET, so not only will they have to rush through the rankings and explanations of whatever dumb thing they did tonight, but fans of that game will either miss the start or have to scramble to find an alternative channel. All of it just puts an annoying cherry on top of what is already an unnecessarily stupid showcase. PSA: The CFP Rankings are supposed to be at 7:30 p.m. They will not be. Because the basketball game preceding it just went to halftime. It’ll likely be after 8. — Chris Vannini (@ChrisVannini) November 24, 2026 It’d be nice if the CFP rankings show were a show that actually started at a specific scheduled time, and not a show that got squeezed in between basketball games every week. — Nicole Auerbach (@NicoleAuerbach) November 25, 2026 Or maybe a little later. After 47 years, you’d think ESPN would know how long a college basketball game takes and schedule accordingly. Yet here we are. — Andy Staples (@AndyStaples) November 25, 2026 When I am CFB Commissioner you will catch the conclusion of Creighton-Michigan on ESPN+ — Josh Pate (@JoshPateCFB) November 25, 2026 Maybe, as some have suggested, the weekly CFP rankings meeting should just be an email . item.title: Phillies in tough spot after failed Teruaki Sato pursuit
item.description: Phillies in tough spot after failed Teruaki Sato pursuit originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Phillies were among the disappointed parties after Teruaki Sato reportedly agreed to a six-year, $120 million contract with the Chicago Cubs . The agreement, reported on Tuesday, leaves the Phillies searching for a middle-of-the-order bat while also extending their drought in signing Japanese players. According to The Philadelphia Inquirer's Scott Lauber , the Phillies offered a multi-year deal to the 27-year-old Japanese slugger before Sato went with the Cubs' $120 million offer. Details of the reported Phillies offer are unknown. Sato was of interest to the Phillies for several reasons. Playing for the Hanshin Tigers, the slugger led Japan's Central League with a .306 batting average, 39 home runs and 106 RBIs. While he is a below-average defender at third base and corner outfield, the Phillies were reportedly ready to play him in left field. After failing to close Sato, the Phillies remain one of the three MLB teams that have yet to sign a player from Nippon Professional Baseball to a major league contract. They were interested in Yoshinobu Yamamoto three years ago, even offering him a deal north of $300 million, but the Japanese ace eventually signed with the Los Angeles Dodgers on a 12-year, $325 million deal. MORE: Why Yankees didn't match Cubs' $120 million offer to Teruaki Sato Phillies' next plan of action after failed Teruaki Sato pursuit After finishing 19th in runs and 22nd in OPS, their lowest marks of the Bryce Harper era (since 2019), Dave Dombrowski & Co. are making efforts to revitalize the Phillies lineup. Their efforts faced a setback on Tuesday after Sato agreed to a deal with the Cubs over the Phillies' multi-year offer. The Phillies' search for a middle-of-the-order right-handed bat to balance out their left-handed-heavy batting lineup could bring them to the doorsteps of Randy Arozarena and Seiya Suzuki. Arozarena recorded his sixth consecutive season with at least 20 home runs and 20 stolen bases in 2026, while also posting a career-best .865 OPS. On the other hand, Suzuki has averaged 24 home runs and an .833 OPS over his last four seasons with the Cubs. The soon-to-be 32-year-olds, who rejected their respective qualifying offers, are seeking a four- or five-year deal this offseason. This may not be the best situation for the Phillies, who will also have to surrender draft-pick compensation and international bonus money to sign either player. In case the Phillies don't want to go in that direction, they may explore a trade with the Dodgers for Teoscar Hernandez. The veteran outfielder will earn $22 million in 2027 and could give the Phillies a right-handed boost to their lineup. item.title: Michigan basketball shot down by Creighton in Players Era opener
item.description: LAS VEGAS — The Wolverines will be glad they won’t have to see another Big East team anytime soon. After falling to UConn three weeks ago and to Villanova this past weekend , Creighton put a quick end to Michigan’s Players Era title defense with a 99-73 blowout loss in the opening round at T-Mobile Arena on Tuesday, Nov. 24. J.P. item.title: US to host 2028 Copa América amid criticism
item.description: FILE PHOTO - A general view of the trophy before the start of the CONMEBOL Copa America 2024 final soccer match between Argentina and Colombia at Hard Rock Stadium. (is associated with: «US to host 2028 Copa América amid criticism») Vanessa Carvalho/ZUMA Press Wire/dpa The United States is set to host the Copa América for a second consecutive edition in 2028, drawing criticism that commercial interests are taking precedence over South American football tradition. South American governing body CONMEBOL and CONCACAF, which oversees football in North and Central America and the Caribbean, confirmed the decision on Tuesday. The US also hosted the 2024 Copa América and the 2025 Club World Cup, as well as most matches at this year's men's World Cup. The Los Angeles Olympics begin just days after the 2028 Copa América ends, while the US is also among the hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup. Ecuador had also expressed interest in staging the tournament for the first time since 1993. The decision drew criticism in South American media and on social media, with Chilean newspaper La Tercera suggesting the competition no longer belonged to South America. US outlet The Athletic also questioned the focus on revenue, arguing that the 110-year-old tournament risked losing cultural significance that money could not replace. First held in 1916, the Copa América is the oldest surviving continental football tournament for national teams. It was staged outside South America for the first time in 2016, also in the US. The 2028 edition is due to take place from June 9 to July 9, featuring all 10 CONMEBOL members and six CONCACAF teams.

item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect College football players: they’re just like us! Each Tuesday, we’re greeted with a new round of seeding for the upcoming College Football Playoff. We’re told these rankings matter, but with the logic and reasoning shifting week to week, it’s hard to see why we’re supposed to care . This year’s logic pretzel around why Alabama has been ahead of Tennessee, even though the Volunteers beat them, is the latest in the long series of confusing decisions . Heck, last year we found out the committee will just reverse its thinking at the last moment if it chooses to. The whole exercise can leave you wondering if you even understand how the College Football Playoff works. And you wouldn’t be alone. Before Georgia’s regular-season finale against Georgia Tech this weekend, DL Joseph Jonah-Ajonye was asked if he or his teammates watch the weekly College Football Playoff Rankings show and think about how it might impact who they play in the first round. To his credit, Jonah-Ajonye has absolutely no idea what you’re talking about. I’m not gonna lie to you, I don’t [watch the rankings show]. If I’m gonna be completely honest, I don’t even know how the playoffs work for real,” Jonah-Ajonye said . “You just line up and play; that’s all I do for real.” Quote of the day comes from UGA DL Joseph Jonah-Ajonye on the CFP rankings. “If I’m gonna be honest, I don’t even know how the playoffs work. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
